source: transcribed 2026-09-26 (S3, set 4) from harness/src/bin/run_engine.rs explain()/rule_record() at e74a503, arm by arm in order; the classes' text verbatim; the tx.* rows and the two classes tx.locktime.discouraged and tx.default-mode.locktime-nops added 2026-09-26 with the tx corpus (Spend.ts at the pin b3155fa2e, read from the ts-stack clone's object) | 2026-09-27 06:5x UTC (S3, the parent; D83): the era-heuristic note (13) moved below the four width rows; the pre-flight on main's recorded data with S3r2's binary (rules.rs knowing spec_consensus): every ts-sdk manifest EQUAL but gen, where the default columns move as the recorded table's own move already showed and further: default/spec no-era 37 -> 35 and width 1 -> 3 (gen-00002 the smallest), default/spec-mempool no-era 5 -> 1, width 4 -> 3, policy 0 -> 5 (gen-00004 the smallest); eras EQUAL; re-read at 2.8.10 for #51/#52 on 2026-10-05, lane harness-b-repin2; re-read at 3.0.0 for #55 on 2026-10-05, lane harness-b-55 (Spend.ts byte-identical to 2.8.10, so every line holds) | 2026-10-06 (lane r34-rules, S3): the owner's rulings on #32 of 2026-10-05: R4, the four default-mode omission classes on the consensus side implementation-wrong with the default-mode scope in each note, the policy-only rows split into flags.default-mode.policy-only (open) by two rows reading spec_consensus; R3, the class engine.decode-refusal and its row (the SDK's decoder, @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Transaction.ts and BigNumber.ts read from the installed package's source map)

bitwise.shift.bigint-limit.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 interpreter.cpp:692–764; script_num.cpp:303–317 at v1.2.3 (the numeric shift result width); [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:1048–1093 (numeric shifts, BigInt result at 1066), 1438–1469 (byte shifts preserve the input width).
bitwise.shift.bigint-limit.note: The default mode has no numeric width bound. A BigInt RangeError is an SDK abort by D15, filed as a witness.

engine.timeout.decided_by: the driver's per-entry wall (harness/src/engines.rs adapter_timeout, ENGINE_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT_S, 120 s by default) and the D15a re-run (2026-09-24, #42): once more in a fresh adapter at ten times the wall; no answer within either, the adapter killed and respawned, both walls named in the message; the reference decides every entry of the generated corpora (corpus/INDEX.md §4c) in milliseconds
engine.timeout.note: the engine returned no verdict on an input the reference decides within the wall and its 10× re-run (D15: an engine that cannot return the verdict disagrees observably; D15a: an entry decided on the re-run carries the engine's verdict and no witness for time alone); a witness, never an undecided run; the entry names the engine's cost, never a semantics

eras.default-mode.no-era.decided_by: [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:319–321, 331–341 (without explicit flags, the eras follow the transaction version); [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 policy.h:226–245, verify_script_flags.cpp:32–81 (coin and spend heights).
eras.default-mode.no-era.note: the default mode has no height input, so the era-boundary rows (a coin or a spend before Genesis, at the Chronicle boundary, at the DERSIG/CLTV/CSV/UAHF/DAA heights, the grandfathered P2SH) are decided by the version heuristic and differ from consensus by construction; reported for the mode's users, never a consensus claim (the explicit-flags columns are the comparable ones)

eras.utxo.spend-bit-conflated.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:411 (utxo_after_genesis = flags & SCRIPT_UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS, the COIN's era bit; policy.h:233–238 sets it per input from the coin's height) against the spend's GENESIS bit (verify_script_flags.cpp:71–75, the block's era); the rules that hang on the coin's era: OP_RETURN 856–871, the 520-byte element 455–458, the 1,000 elements 1800–1803, the 500 ops 466–467, the 4-byte numbers (script_num.cpp:62 with configscriptpolicy.cpp:83–86), the 10,000-byte script 429–430, the 20 keys (consensus.h:50), the disabled opcodes in a dead branch 470–471, the second OP_ELSE 829–831; ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:326–335 (#isAfterGenesis with explicit flags = GENESIS || UTXO_AFTER_GENESIS || UTXO_AFTER_CHRONICLE) read at 387–392 (the number width), 743–750 and 794–805 (the disabled opcodes), 1110–1114 (the single ELSE), 1142–1145 (OP_RETURN), 1642 (the key count) and the limits 23–27
eras.utxo.spend-bit-conflated.note: the engine reads the coin's era from the spend's GENESIS bit, so a coin created before Genesis and spent in any later block is judged under the post-Genesis rules in the explicit-flags mode: the pre-Genesis limits and rules the reference applies to that coin (the eras corpus's pre-genesis rows) are not applied, and the post-Genesis single-ELSE rule is applied where the reference allows the second OP_ELSE

expansion.rshiftnum.negative-rounding.decided_by: script_num.cpp:340–352 (the int64 path: `-((-value) >> bit_shift)`, division by 2^count rounding toward zero) and the big-int path (the magnitude shifted, the sign kept: big_int.cpp:371–393); the spec's own SV-node instance agrees with the spec on gen-00829 (−3 OP_RSHIFTNUM 3 = 0; corpus/INDEX.md §4c); go-sdk v1.5.2 operations.go:2569–2575 (big.Int.Rsh on the signed value: an arithmetic shift, −3 >> 3 = −1)
expansion.rshiftnum.negative-rounding.note: a negative number shifted right by the engine rounds toward negative infinity where the reference rounds toward zero: a spend the reference accepts (the result 0 compared by OP_EQUAL) fails on the engine

expansion.shift.count-bigint.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:708–711 and 744–747 (the count as CScriptNum{…, true}, the big-int path), big_int.cpp:359–369 and 383–393 (a bint count that does not fit an int throws big_int_error) → interpreter.cpp:1819–1821 SCRIPT_ERR_BIG_INT; the spec's own SV-node instance says SCRIPT_ERR_BIG_INT on gen-00835 (corpus/INDEX.md §4c); go-sdk v1.5.2 operations.go:2547–2575 (the count capped at MaxScriptNumberLengthAfterChronicle × 8 and shifted, never refused); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:947–978 (value << bits / value >> bits as BigInts, a negative count alone refused)
expansion.shift.count-bigint.note: the engine shifts by a count the reference refuses as outside int (SCRIPT_ERR_BIG_INT): a right shift by 2^31 is 0 to the engine and a refusal on the reference

flags.discourage-upgradable-nops.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 policy.h:186 (policy flag); interpreter.cpp:765–771; [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:839, 887 (DISCOURAGE_UPGRADABLE_NOPS).
flags.discourage-upgradable-nops.note: a POLICY flag: the relay word refuses an executed upgradable NOP, the block word and the default mode accept it; not a consensus divergence

flags.policy-as-consensus.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 policy.h:178–190; verify_script_flags.cpp:32–81 (standard restrictions absent from the block word); [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:319–321, 347–374 (default restrictions by transaction version).
flags.policy-as-consensus.note: the SDK's default mode judges a version-1 spend by the relay restrictions no block word carries: a mode, not a claim about consensus; an application that validates blocks with the default mode rejects consensus-valid version-1 spends

flags.version-gate.absent.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:40–44 EnforceNonMalleability(flags, v) = !(IsChronicle(flags) && v > 1) at the seven sites 285 (LOW_S), 433 (MINIMALDATA), 801 (MINIMALIF), 1493 and 1643 (NULLFAIL), 1666 (NULLDUMMY), 2441 (CLEANSTACK) and the SIGPUSHONLY read at 2327; go-sdk v1.5.2 scriptflag/scriptflag.go:1–86 (no spend-era flag: SCRIPT_CHRONICLE and SCRIPT_GENESIS have no image), thread.go:232 (clean stack), 342 (push-only), 753 (high S), operations.go:2059/2301 (NULLFAIL), 2178 (NULLDUMMY), 408/411 (MINIMALIF), opcodeparser.go:95–129 and number.go:424 (minimal data), every one on the flag alone; ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:341–366 (#shouldEnforceMinimalData/LowS/NullDummy/SigPushOnly/CleanStack return #hasFlag(...) when explicit flags are given, the transaction version never read), 1090–1096 (MINIMALIF), 1613/1737 (NULLFAIL)
flags.version-gate.absent.note: under a post-Chronicle word (CHRONICLE set) the reference turns MINIMALDATA, LOW_S, NULLFAIL, NULLDUMMY, MINIMALIF, CLEANSTACK and SIGPUSHONLY off for a transaction of version > 1; the engine applies each whenever its flag is set: a consensus-valid version-2 spend is refused under the node's own word (the block word carries LOW_S, NULLFAIL and SIGPUSHONLY; the relay word all seven)

flags.version-gate.nullfail.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 interpreter.cpp:1491–1497,1641–1647; standard.h:62–68; @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:1710–1715,1844–1849 (NULLFAIL requires an explicit flag name and the version gate); Spend.ts:327–329 (the default mode has no flag names).
flags.version-gate.nullfail.note: the default mode accepts a version-1 spend with a failing non-empty signature that the reference's word refuses at the spend's height. Scope (the owner's ruling R4 on #32, 2026-10-05, road 1): implementation-wrong in the SDK's DEFAULT MODE only, @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 called without verifyFlags, in this harness's default/spec and default/spec-mempool columns on the corpora named in corpus/witnesses/ts-sdk/manifest.json at the reference pin bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 (879fc8b); the explicit-flags columns are judged by their own rows, and no claim is made of a mode or a version not run. A row the block word accepts and only the relay word refuses is flags.default-mode.policy-only, never this class.

flow.else.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 interpreter.cpp:829–831; conditional_tracker.cpp:51–55; @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:1191–1202 (the single-ELSE test requires explicit flags and a post-Genesis coin; the default mode toggles again).
flow.else.note: the default mode (no explicit word) accepts a second OP_ELSE the reference refuses post-Genesis. Scope (the owner's ruling R4 on #32, 2026-10-05, road 1): implementation-wrong in the SDK's DEFAULT MODE only, @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 called without verifyFlags, in this harness's default/spec and default/spec-mempool columns on the corpora named in corpus/witnesses/ts-sdk/manifest.json at the reference pin bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 (879fc8b); the explicit-flags columns are judged by their own rows, and no claim is made of a mode or a version not run.

limits.maxscriptnumlength.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 script_num.cpp:62; interpreter.cpp:1789–1790, 1807–1810; configscriptpolicy.cpp:79–110; consensus.h:62–66; [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:395–403 (explicit numeric reads: 4, 750000, 32000000 bytes; default unlimited), 1989–1997 (OP_BIN2NUM omits the size argument), 107–111 (helper default Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER).
limits.maxscriptnumlength.note: The explicit numeric reads enforce the consensus widths. OP_BIN2NUM does not pass that width to its result test; the default mode has no number width. A policy-only refusal is classified separately.

limits.maxscriptnumlength.policy.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 configscriptpolicy.cpp:79–110; policy.h:156 (default policy width 10000 bytes); consensus.h:64, 66 (consensus widths); interpreter.cpp:1789–1790, 1807–1810; [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:395–403 (consensus widths on numeric reads, no policy input), 1989–1997 (OP_BIN2NUM result test has no width).
limits.maxscriptnumlength.policy.note: A policy width, kept separate from consensus: the node relay default refuses numbers above 10000 bytes that its block word accepts; the SDK has no policy width parameter.

sighash.default-mode.forkid-not-required.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 interpreter.cpp:304–306; verify_script_flags.cpp:56–58; [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:595–603 (the default mode returns before enforcing FORKID).
sighash.default-mode.forkid-not-required.note: the default mode accepts a signature without the FORKID bit that the reference's block word refuses before verifying at every spend height from the UAHF on. Scope (the owner's ruling R4 on #32, 2026-10-05, road 1): implementation-wrong in the SDK's DEFAULT MODE only, @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 called without verifyFlags, in this harness's default/spec and default/spec-mempool columns on the corpora named in corpus/witnesses/ts-sdk/manifest.json at the reference pin bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 (879fc8b); the explicit-flags columns are judged by their own rows, and no claim is made of a mode or a version not run. A row the block word accepts and only the relay word refuses (a spend below the UAHF height) is flags.default-mode.policy-only, never this class.

sighash.dispatch.forkid-bit-without-flag.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:2112–2124 (SignatureHash: the BIP143 digest iff SCRIPT_ENABLE_SIGHASH_FORKID is in the flags AND the type has the FORKID bit, 2118–2121; the original digest otherwise), verify_script_flags.cpp:32–59 (no FORKID flag in the block word before the UAHF height 478,559), 291 and 302–303 (the FORKID bit is refused only under STRICTENC, absent from that word); the spec's own SV-node instance accepts gen-00995 on both instances; go-sdk v1.5.2 transaction/signaturehash.go:19–26 (the FORKID BIT alone selects the BIP143 preimage, else the legacy one) and 90–92 (the cached path the same)
sighash.dispatch.forkid-bit-without-flag.note: a pre-UAHF spend whose hash type carries the FORKID bit is hashed the original way by the reference and accepted; the engine hashes it as BIP143 and the signature fails: the flag has no part in its dispatch

sighash.must-use-forkid.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:305–306 (SCRIPT_ERR_MUST_USE_FORKID when the word enables FORKID and the signature's hash type lacks the bit; under STRICTENC, which 2314–2318 forces whenever FORKID is enabled), verify_script_flags.cpp:56–58 (both bits from the UAHF height, 478,559 on mainnet); go-sdk v1.5.2 script/interpreter/thread.go:528–558 checkHashTypeEncoding: a hash type without ForkID whose base type is defined returns nil at 541–546, so the EnableSighashForkID-without-ForkID refusal at 555–556 (ErrIllegalForkID, the table's MUST_USE_FORKID row) is unreachable for the case it names
sighash.must-use-forkid.note: the reference refuses the spend before verifying the signature; the engine verifies it and judges the spend by the outcome (here a failing signature under OP_CHECKSIG OP_NOT: valid under the block word, NULLFAIL under the relay word); a consensus-invalid spend accepted under the node's own block word

sighash.original.truncated-push.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:1862–1892 (SerializeScriptCode: the size prefix counts the whole scriptCode minus the OP_CODESEPARATORs parsed, the bytes stop at the parser's failure point after the opcode and a whole length prefix; script.h:163–196 GetOp2) reached through the original digest (2123; the CHRONICLE bit, Q2) for a lock `<pk> OP_CHECKSIG OP_RETURN <a truncated push>` whose top-level OP_RETURN terminates a post-Genesis script successfully with the rest unparsed (856–871); the spec's own SV-node instance agrees with the spec on all six shapes (corpus/INDEX.md §4c, 2026-09-24); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:1552–1564 (the scriptCode built from the parsed chunks of the locking script and re-serialized; the chunks are the lazy parser's, Script.#parseChunks, not Script.fromBinary's, which only stores the bytes: at 3.0.0 Script.ts:157–160 and 599, whose top-level OP_RETURN branch 608–611 takes the rest of the script as one data chunk, so this class's truncated push after the top-level OP_RETURN is never read as a push; the adapter builds the lock from hex, LockingScript.fromHex, harness/engines/ts/runner.mjs:84) and 1565 (findAndDelete on the chunks): the digest differs on five of the six shapes (the lone PUSHDATA1 opcode, gen-00997, survives), so the signature fails (NULLFAIL under a word that carries it, a false top otherwise)
sighash.original.truncated-push.note: a spend the reference accepts (the signature over the reference's serialization of an unparseable scriptCode) fails on the engine: the engine's re-serialization of a truncated push is not the reference's byte walk; the BIP143 twins (the scriptCode hashed whole) agree

sighash.scriptcode.findanddelete.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:255–263 CleanupScriptCode (no FindAndDelete when FORKID is enabled and in the hash type), 1484; ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:1604 (OP_CHECKSIG) and 1689 (OP_CHECKMULTISIG): subscript.findAndDelete(the signature) unconditionally
sighash.scriptcode.findanddelete.note: the signature's own push is deleted from the scriptCode under FORKID, so a signature over the deleted scriptCode verifies where the reference hashes the push in and refuses the spend

sighash.type.chronicle-bit.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:291–303 (under STRICTENC an undefined hash type is SIG_HASHTYPE, the CHRONICLE bit is legal iff the word carries SCRIPT_CHRONICLE: ILLEGAL_CHRONICLE before, accepted after) with sighashtype.h:14–22 (SIGHASH_CHRONICLE = 0x20) and 2112–2124 (the original digest for a Chronicle-bit signature); go-sdk v1.5.2 transaction/sighash/flag.go:18–26 (ForkID 0x40 and AnyOneCanPay 0x80 are the only high bits; no 0x20) and script/interpreter/thread.go:548–549 (a hash type above SingleForkID 0x43 is ErrInvalidSigHashType); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:533–542 (#enforceSignatureHashType: the CHRONICLE bit is legal iff #isAfterChronicle(), which with explicit flags is the COIN's UTXO_AFTER_CHRONICLE at 337–339, where the reference reads the SPEND's SCRIPT_CHRONICLE at interpreter.cpp:298; the refusal is thrown inside the try of #checkSignatureEncoding 563–575 and re-labelled 'The signature format is invalid' by its catch)
sighash.type.chronicle-bit.note: a version-2 spend post-Chronicle whose signature carries the CHRONICLE bit is consensus-valid on the reference (the eras corpus's chronicle-bit rows at 943,816 and above); go-sdk refuses it as an undefined hash type under the node's own words, block and relay alike; ts-sdk refuses it whenever the COIN was created before Chronicle, whatever block spends it, reporting a format error

sighash.type.forkid-bit.pre-genesis.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:291 (the hash-type checks run under SCRIPT_VERIFY_STRICTENC alone), 302–303 (SCRIPT_ERR_ILLEGAL_FORKID: the FORKID bit without SCRIPT_ENABLE_SIGHASH_FORKID); the block word before the UAHF carries neither (verify_script_flags.cpp:32–59), so the reference verifies the signature over the original digest and accepts it (the node on gen-00995); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:509–515 (#enforceSignatureForkId: 'must not use SIGHASH_FORKID' when the FORKID flag is absent, the coin is pre-Genesis and the type has the bit) called from #checkSignatureEncoding's try (526–537) whenever DER signatures are enforced (DERSIG, LOW_S or STRICTENC), the refusal re-labelled 'The signature format is invalid' by its catch
sighash.type.forkid-bit.pre-genesis.note: a pre-UAHF spend the reference accepts under its own block word (DERSIG on, STRICTENC off) is refused by the engine: a STRICTENC-gated check applied under DERSIG

splice.num2bin.memory.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:1749–1752 (OP_NUM2BIN refuses a size above INT32_MAX with SCRIPT_ERR_PUSH_SIZE before anything is built), 1771–1777 with configscriptpolicy.cpp:139–154 (the consensus memory budget INT64_MAX); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:391–395 (#maxPushSize is Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY after Genesis: no bound below 2^32), 1816–1836 (a size up to 0xffffffff reaches Array.from({length: size}); above it ScriptResourceLimitError)
splice.num2bin.memory.note: a width of 2^31 the reference refuses with PUSH_SIZE makes the SDK allocate the element and V8 abort the process (`FATAL ERROR: invalid table size Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`, node 22, 1.7 GB resident, deterministic in a fresh process); a 40,000,000-byte element the reference builds within its budget is built by the SDK in a fresh process (about 0.8 GB resident) and has killed a long-lived adapter process once under batching (recovered by the harness's retry in a fresh process). A resource wall and a process death, never a verdict: an abort by D15, a witness (never an undecided run since 2026-09-24)

splice.substr.int64-reader.decided_by: The reading of record at v1.2.3 is a defined refusal ([SRC] `int_serialization.h:61–118`, `script_num.cpp:80–91` at `6504a3af`); the previous pin's reading and its measurements are recorded in material withheld from the public edition at the maintainers' request (group `d8-node-team-discretion`). [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 `Spend.ts:539–562` reads the lower eight bytes above that width, uses BigInt.asIntN(64), and clamps.
splice.substr.int64-reader.note: The reading of record at v1.2.3 is a defined refusal ([SRC] `int_serialization.h:61–118`, `script_num.cpp:80–91` at `6504a3af`); the previous pin's reading and its measurements are recorded in material withheld from the public edition at the maintainers' request (group `d8-node-team-discretion`).

tx.locktime.nop.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:519–560 (OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY executes for a pre-Genesis UTXO: the checker's CheckLockTime 2166–2202; a NOP for a post-Genesis UTXO 520–526); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:1016–1019 (OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY falls through to break in every mode; the CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY name is never read: the run's manifest counts it among the names the engine has no flag for)
tx.locktime.nop.note: a pre-Genesis coin's CLTV lock is never enforced by the engine: a spend the reference refuses as SCRIPT_ERR_UNSATISFIED_LOCKTIME is valid to it under the node's own words

tx.sequence.check-absent.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:562–597 (OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY for a pre-Genesis UTXO: the checker's CheckSequence 2204–2250 compares the masked operand with the input's nSequence, the transaction's version and the disable bit); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:1021–1050 (under the CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY flag: the operand's sign, the disable bit and the version only; the input's sequence is never read)
tx.sequence.check-absent.note: a pre-Genesis coin's relative lock is never compared with the input's sequence by the engine: a spend the reference refuses as SCRIPT_ERR_UNSATISFIED_LOCKTIME is valid to it under the node's own words

tx.sequence.post-genesis-utxo.decided_by: interpreter.cpp:562–597 (OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY executes for a pre-Genesis UTXO only; for a post-Genesis UTXO 563–569: a NOP, discouraged under the policy flag); ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:1020–1050 (executed whenever the CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY name is given, the UTXO era never read; the check is the version and the disable bit only, never the input's sequence)
tx.sequence.post-genesis-utxo.note: under a word carrying CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY (every block and relay word since CSVHeight) a post-Genesis spend that leaves a number without the disable bit under OP_NOP3 is refused for a version-1 transaction where the reference treats the opcode as a NOP; OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY is a NOP in every mode (Spend.ts:1016–1018): the pre-Genesis families of #26 exhibit that one

tx.locktime.discouraged.decided_by: ts-sdk 2.8.0 Spend.ts:818–832 (#enforceDiscouragedNop: under DISCOURAGE_UPGRADABLE_NOPS an executing OP_NOP1, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY, OP_NOP9 or OP_NOP10 is refused as "discouraged by verification flags", the coin's era never read); the reference executes OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY and OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY for a pre-Genesis coin (interpreter.cpp:519–597) and treats them as NOPs discouraged by the policy flag only for a post-Genesis coin (520–526 and 563–569)
tx.locktime.discouraged.note: under the node's own relay word a valid spend of a pre-Genesis coin through OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY or OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY is refused by the engine (the tx.* corpus, 2026-09-26); the block word carries no DISCOURAGE flag, so there the same opcodes are NOPs to the engine (tx.locktime.nop, tx.sequence.check-absent)

tx.default-mode.locktime-nops.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 interpreter.cpp:522–597; [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:892–931 (CLTV and CSV require explicit flag names), 327–329 (no flag names in the default mode).
tx.default-mode.locktime-nops.note: (a class under a still-private advisory: withheld, D135) (withheld until the advisory publishes). Scope (the owner's ruling R4 on #32, 2026-10-05, road 1): implementation-wrong in the SDK's DEFAULT MODE only, @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 called without verifyFlags, in this harness's default/spec and default/spec-mempool columns on the corpora named in corpus/witnesses/ts-sdk/manifest.json at the reference pin bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 (879fc8b); the explicit-flags columns are judged by their own rows, and no claim is made of a mode or a version not run.

engine.decode-refusal.decided_by: [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Transaction.ts:548–553 (fromHex), 497 (every output amount through readUInt64LEBn().toNumber()), BigNumber.ts:625–629 (toNumber throws above 2^53: 'Number can only safely store up to 53 bits'); [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 validation.cpp:543–546 (the reference decodes the amount as an int64 and decides the transaction at its own checks); D15 (docs/DESIGN.md §2.1).
engine.decode-refusal.note: The owner's ruling R3 on #32 (2026-10-05, road 1: D15 as written): the SDK's own decoder refuses a corpus transaction the reference decodes and the spec decides, so the engine returns no script verdict where the spec has one: an engine abort under D15, implementation-wrong, the engine's script status undecided (engine-undecided), the recorded script verdict kept, counted once as a witness and never as an undecided run as well. The script verdict and the transaction's validity are distinct: this class does not establish an engine failure on a transaction the reference would accept (the corpus's row is one the reference refuses at its transaction checks). Scoped to @bsv/sdk 3.0.0, every column, the corpora of corpus/witnesses/ts-sdk/manifest.json and the pin.

flags.default-mode.policy-only.decided_by: [SRC] bitcoin-sv v1.2.2 verify_script_flags.cpp:32–81 (the block word by the spend height: SIGHASH_FORKID from the UAHF, 56–58), policy.h:178–190 and standard.h:62–68 (the relay word's standard flags at every height); interpreter.cpp:304–306, 1491–1497, 1641–1647 (MUST_USE_FORKID, NULLFAIL); [SRC] @bsv/sdk 3.0.0 Spend.ts:595–603, 1710–1715, 1844–1849 (FORKID and NULLFAIL only under explicit flag names), 327–329 (no flag names in the default mode).
